text:
Kiran Patel: Quick follow-up on the resume-lite handshake we sketched — need to reconcile retries, tenant fairness, and billing.

Marie Lopez: Can you restate the main constraint? I remember we wanted small state at the edge but also reliable mid-stream resumption.

Kiran Patel: TL;DR: propose a thin resume token (opaque pointer + checksum) that lets the edge avoid replaying full prefix. Add a per-request retry budget header so we can account for retry attempts across the gateway and upstream.

Samir Rao: 👍 but memory pressure is my top worry. We can't keep full checkpoints for thousands of concurrent clients. Suggest the token references an ephemeral store entry (LRU + TTL) sharded by tenant. If the entry is evicted we do a cold retry.

Marie Lopez: Evicting -> cold retry has side effects for idempotent vs non-idempotent requests. We need clear semantics and a way to surface "progress lost" to the client. :thinking:

Anya K: Agreed. Clients should be able to detect and adapt. Propose a trailer or final flag that indicates whether resume succeeded or we fell back to replay/cold.

Kiran Patel: Draft header/trailer proposal:

- Request headers:
  - `X-RW-Resume-Token: <opaque>`
  - `X-RW-Retry-Budget: <int>`
  - `X-RW-Tenant-ID: <tenant>` (existing but calling out for clarity)
- Response trailer:
  - `x-rw-resume-progress: partial|lost|complete`
- Tracing tag:
  - `rw.resume.evicted=true|false`

Example usage:

```
curl -H "X-RW-Resume-Token: abc123" \
     -H "X-RW-Retry-Budget: 2" \
     https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/generate --no-buffer
```

Jim O'Neill: For fairness, shard the resume store by tenant and track `active-resume-count`. If a tenant hits quota, deny creating new resume entries (return short-lived `resume-denied` hint) and fall back to standard retry. Metric: `resume.denied.tenant=<id>`.

gateway-bot: Canary plan outline:
- Feature flag: `edge.resume_lite` (off by default)
- Rollout: 10% tenants -> 25% -> 100%
- Metrics to watch: `resume.success`, `resume.evicted`, `resume.denied`, `resume.fallback_cold`, `resume.latency_p50/p95`

Marie Lopez: Billing question — if we resume mid-stream, how do we avoid double-billing the prefix tokens? Suggest we record a `billing.checkpoint_ts` with each resume entry and only bill deltas after successful resume confirmation.

Samir Rao: Implementation note: resumed streams should reuse the kvcache and avoid reparsing the prefix frames where possible. That means we need a small canonicalization step when storing a resume entry so the runtime can reattach quickly.

Anya K: Client-visible schema: I can draft a minimal trailer proto that encodes `{progress: enum, prefix_consumed: int}` and a human-readable message. Will share by EOD.

Kiran Patel: Action items:
- Samir: draft storage design (TTL, eviction, shard quotas).
- Marie: draft billing contract with finance for checkpoint/delta billing.
- Anya: propose trailer proto + client guidance.
- Jim: prototype tenant fairness counters & deny path.
- I'll open RFC follow-up PR with header names, sample curl, and canary plan.

Kiran Patel: Also: keep `X-RW-Retry-Budget` decremented by proxies upstream so we don't exceed allowed retries across layers. If budget hits 0, proxies should stop hedging automatically.

Jim O'Neill: Another thought — expose `resume.store.utilization` per-tenant to the console so SRE/product can tune quotas during rollout.

gateway-bot: Noted. Will add metrics checklist to the rollout doc.

Anya K: Ack — I'll put a sketch in the RFC branch.

Marie Lopez: One more quick concern: RTT-sensitive clients might prefer immediate cold retry to avoid waiting for resume lookup. We should make the client opt-in for resume via header presence; default remains no-resume.

Kiran Patel: Good call. We'll keep resume opt-in. Thanks everyone. :+1:
